title: Coordinate rapid PRD clarifications, legal spot-checks, and acceptance micro-lanes
creator: Priya Patel
description: Problem: PRD 'Scoped Structured Output V2' has several interdependent clarifications required between engineering, design, and legal. Current handoff cadence (weekly review) causes >48h blocking for signoffs and leads to scope creep during last-mile changes. Goal: Define a lightweight, repeatable micro-lane process that enables rapid clarifications (<=24h turnaround for trivial items), deterministic legal spot-checks for data residency/consent language, and explicit acceptance criteria so rollouts are not delayed by ambiguous ownership.
acceptance_criteria: A1: All open PRD clarification items are triaged into 'micro' (<=24h) or 'macro' (>24h) lanes and documented in the PRD comments section.
A2: Legal confirms required spot-check checklist items for the PRD within 48 hours of a 'micro' lane tag or explicitly escalates to legal-review lane.
A3: Design and Engineering provide a signed-off checklist entry for each micro-lane item; status must be ‘Design OK’ and ‘Eng OK’ before PM marks the PRD acceptance item resolved.
A4: Any change to rollout acceptance criteria must include rollback triggers and customer-impact assessment before acceptance is final.
A5: The micro-lane runbook is published in Confluence and referenced in the PRD; three pilot PRDs use the process with post-mortem notes collected.
A6: No more than one production-blocking ambiguity remains unresolved at release decision time for the scoped PRD.
runbook_steps: Step 1: Triage meeting (15 min) with PM/Eng/Design/Legal to categorize outstanding clarifications as micro/macro.
Step 2: Create a PRD sub-section 'CLARIFICATIONS' and add discrete tickets (micro-lane labels) with owners and due timestamps.

Step 3: Legal runs a predefined spot-check list (data residency, consent text, logging retention) for items flagged as touching customer data; legal to update ticket with 'Legal: OK' or 'Legal: escalate'.
Step 4: Engineering attaches a short implementation note and risk level (none/minor/major) and indicates required runtime changes or migration windows.
Step 5: Design attaches annotated screenshots or component notes for UX acceptance; if UX diff is large, move to macro lane.
Step 6: PM performs final validation against acceptance criteria and schedules release gating call if any macro items remain.
Step 7: After release decision, collect micro-lane post-mortem: time-to-resolution metrics and one improvement action.
Fallback: If any micro item slips past 48h, escalate to Head of Product (Priya) and the cross-functional standing meeting.
Metrics captured: time-to-triage, time-to-legal-ok, percent micro-lane success within SLA, number of scope changes introduced during last 7 days before release.
